page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6e-c12g1.12xlarge is a GPU-accelerated compute instance powered by the KVM hypervisor on the x86_64 architecture. The server features 48 dedicated vCPUs derived from 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, supported by 33 MB of L3 cache. System memory totals 368.0 GB, yielding 7.67 GB per physical core. For parallel acceleration, the instance integrates four NVIDIA Volta V100 GPUs providing a combined 128 GB of VRAM. Networking includes a baseline bandwidth of 16 Gbps, while local instance storage is absent, necessitating network-attached block storage for persistence.

Benchmark results highlight an emphasis on parallel throughput over single-threaded execution. In CPU stress tests, single-core performance scores in the bottom quartile at 1110.4, and single-threaded compression speeds under gzip and bzip3 are similarly constrained. Conversely, multi-threaded stress-ng throughput reaches average tiers at 35520.27, matched by an average multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 147.7 GB/sec. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth measures 98.85 GB/sec, large-block write bandwidth reaches 47.39 GB/sec, and cached small-block read bandwidth attains 1975.99 GB/sec. In application-level metrics, Redis SET throughput registers at 33.18 million operations per second and static web throughput hits 23.02 GB/sec.

The hardware profile represents a specialized resource distribution tailored toward GPU-dense parallel computations rather than per-core compute efficiency. Because single-thread performance is modest and local storage is not bundled, workloads relying on fast local I/O or sequential CPU speeds will encounter bottlenecks. However, the substantial GPU memory footprint and balanced system RAM enable dense batch processing and multi-GPU computing.
Primary workload fits include distributed deep learning training, GPU-based batch inference, scientific modeling, molecular dynamics simulations, and parallel matrix operations.
